subject: Pegasus AI renewal — request for special consideration on pricing & SLA
messages:
From: Tom Conway <tom.conway@pegasus.ai>
To: ava_chen@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Contract renewal and pricing discussion

Ava —

We have the renewal coming up for Pegasus on Oct 1. Usage this quarter is down ~30% vs. forecast due to a pause in one product line. Given that, procurement is pushing back on the current renewal numbers and asking for a meaningful reduction or credits tied to the lower consumption.

Can we get a path to a reduced price or credits for Q3 usage so we can keep moving forward without escalating? We’d prefer to stay on Redwood — the tech fit has been great — but the budget gatekeepers are strict.

Thanks,
Tom
VP, Platform Engineering
Pegasus AI
From: ava_chen@redwood.ai
To: Tom Conway <tom.conway@pegasus.ai>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Contract renewal and pricing discussion

Tom —

Thanks for the note and for the heads up on procurement. I’ve looped in Lauren from Customer Success to capture usage details and start a short MA
P (mutual action plan), and I’ll escalate to the deal desk so we can explore options.

At a high level, we can consider a short-term usage credit and a 12-month term reset with a stepped pricing profile, or an SLA add-on to address the reliability concerns that were raised. Before I take this to finance/leadership, could you confirm: 1) expected annual committed spend if we keep them on a 12-month renewal with credits, and 2) whether they require contract language changes (data residency or KMS) beyond our standard terms?

If you can share a quick usage export and the procurement wishlist, I’ll compile an ask and propose options.

— Ava Chen
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
To: ava_chen@redwood.ai, Tom Conway <tom.conway@pegasus.ai>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Contract renewal and pricing discussion

Tom / Ava —

I attached a quick Q3 usage export (pegasus_usage_q3.csv) and a short summary of top offending routes. Key callouts: overall token volume down 31%, but latency-sensitive inference for search is still high-value and has spiky peaks. Procurement asked specifically for: (a) a one-time usage credit to offset Q3 underutilization, (b) a 12-month term reset so they don’t have to reforecast mid-year, and (c) an SLA addendum for higher uptime on search inference with a small credits bucket.

Tom — I flagged the most important routes in column D. Happy to join the deal desk conversation.

Regards,
Lauren Bishop
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
To: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, ava_chen@redwood.ai
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Pegasus renewal — executive ask for concession authorization

Team —

I reviewed the ask from Pegasus. Summary of requested concessions: 15% one-time credit on Q3 invoice, 12-month term reset with 10% introductory discount in month 1–3, and a Platinum SLA add-on (0.5% monthly credit pool on breach). Current ARR for Pegasus is $620k; expected committed spend under the reset is $560k.

Given the strategic fit and the risk of churn (they are in active PoC with two other vendors for a small pilot), I recommend we authorize up to a $45k total concession budget (credits + first-year discount) with the following controls:
- Credit applied only after they sign the renewed 12-month term and provide a PO.
- SLA addendum accepted as a 6-month pilot, after which we revisit metrics.
- Escalation: anything above $45k requires VP sign-off.

Please review — Marcus, I need finance sign-off on the $45k ceiling and confirmation this structure works for revenue recognition and ARR. Ava, please confirm the customer's committed spend and whether the procurement asks for nonstandard legal clauses. I’m aiming to finalize an executive-level approval to send a formal proposal by EOD Pacific.

— Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, ava_chen@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 10:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pegasus renewal — executive ask for concession authorization

Vivek —

Finance reviewed the proposed concession budget and timing. We can approve up to $45,000 total provided the following are enforced:
1) Credit is recognized as contra-revenue and amortized over the 12-month term for ARR calculations.
2) Procurement must submit a signed PO and the renewal contract must include standard Redwood terms; any nonstandard legal language will void the pre-approval and require legal review.
3) SLA pilot limited to 6 months and capped exposure at $25k in credit payouts over that period.

Assuming Ava confirms the $560k committed spend, I authorize the deal desk to proceed with the formal proposal under those controls. I’ve attached a short concession summary (proposed_concession_summary.pdf) for the executive packet.

Marcus Lin
Director, Finance — Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Tom / Priya —

Appreciate your patience. Per our internal approvals, here is the proposal we can move forward with if Pegasus signs by Sep 24 and issues a PO:

Offer summary:
- One-time Q3 usage credit: 15% of the invoiced Q3 usage (applied as a credit on first invoice after renewal)
- Term: 12-month reset at the agreed committed spend level of $560,000 ARR
- Introductory pricing: 10% discount for the first 3 months of the reset term
- SLA addendum: 6-month pilot for Platinum SLA with a 0.5% monthly credits pool for breaches, capped at $25k over the pilot

Controls and conditions:
- Credit and discounts require a signed renewal and PO.
- No changes to standard Redwood legal terms without legal review.
- Credit is amortized for ARR and finance visibility.

Next steps: If you’re aligned, we’ll prepare a redlined contract reflecting these bullets and route for signatures. Lauren, I’ll hand off the MA
P and onboarding notes once they sign.

Thanks — I’ll be on standby for any procurement questions.

Best,
Ava Chen

Redwood Inference
